passages.text: You yourselves know, brothers, that our visit to you was not in vain.
passages.sermon:
Paul and his companions visited the Thessalonian believers.
Paul calls the Thessalonians "brothers."
The Thessalonians know about Paul's visit.
Paul's visit to the Thessalonians was not empty.
Paul's visit had real purpose and effect.
passages.original: Αὐτοὶ γὰρ οἴδατε ἀδελφοί τὴν εἴσοδον ἡμῶν τὴν πρὸς ὑμᾶς ὅτι οὐ κενὴ γέγονεν

passages.text: As you are aware, we had already endured suffering and shameful treatment in Philippi. But in the face of strong opposition, we were bold in our God to speak to you the gospel of God.
passages.sermon:
We are apostles of Jesus Christ.
You know what happened to us in Philippi.
We suffered in Philippi.
People treated us shamefully in Philippi.
You are aware of this.
We faced strong opposition.
Even so, we spoke to you with boldness.
God gave us courage.
We preached the gospel of God to you.
We did this while struggling greatly.
passages.original: ἀλλὰ προπαθόντες καὶ ὑβρισθέντες καθὼς οἴδατε ἐν Φιλίπποις ἐπαρρησιασάμεθα ἐν τῷ Θεῷ ἡμῶν λαλῆσαι πρὸς ὑμᾶς τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐν πολλῷ ἀγῶνι

passages.text: For our appeal does not arise from deceit or ulterior motives or trickery.
passages.sermon:
We make our appeal to you.
We do not use deceit.
We do not have impure motives.
We do not act with trickery.
passages.original: Ἡ γὰρ παράκλησις ἡμῶν οὐκ ἐκ πλάνης οὐδὲ ἐξ ἀκαθαρσίας οὐδὲ ἐν δόλῳ

passages.text: Instead, we speak as those approved by God to be entrusted with the gospel, not in order to please men but God, who examines our hearts.
passages.sermon:
God approved us.
God entrusted us with the gospel.
We speak because God gave us this trust.
We do not try to please people.
We try to please God.
God examines our hearts.
passages.original: ἀλλὰ καθὼς δεδοκιμάσμεθα ὑπὸ τοῦ Θεοῦ πιστευθῆναι τὸ εὐαγγέλιον οὕτως λαλοῦμεν οὐχ ὡς ἀνθρώποις ἀρέσκοντες ἀλλὰ Θεῷ τῷ δοκιμάζοντι τὰς καρδίας ἡμῶν

passages.text: As you know, we never used words of flattery or any pretext for greed. God is our witness!
passages.sermon:
We are apostles of Christ.
We spoke to you.
You know this.
We never used words of flattery.
We never spoke to gain anything for ourselves.
We did not use any pretext for greed.
God is our witness.
passages.original: οὔτε γάρ ποτε ἐν λόγῳ κολακείας ἐγενήθημεν καθὼς οἴδατε οὔτε ἐν προφάσει πλεονεξίας Θεὸς μάρτυς

passages.text: Nor did we seek praise from you or from anyone else, although as apostles of Christ we had authority to demand it.
passages.sermon:
We are apostles of Christ.
We have authority from Christ.
We did not seek praise from you.
We did not seek praise from anyone else.
We did not use our authority to make demands.
passages.original: οὔτε ζητοῦντες ἐξ ἀνθρώπων δόξαν οὔτε ἀφ’ ὑμῶν οὔτε ἀπ’ ἄλλων δυνάμενοι ἐν βάρει εἶναι ὡς Χριστοῦ ἀπόστολοι

passages.text: On the contrary, we were gentle among you, like a nursing mother caring for her children.
passages.sermon:
We were apostles of Christ.
We lived among you.
We acted with gentleness.
We did not act harshly.
We were gentle, just as a nursing mother cares for her own children.
We cared for you with tenderness.
We showed you kindness and love.
passages.original: Ἀλλὰ ἐγενήθημεν ἤπιοι ἐν μέσῳ ὑμῶν ὡς ἐὰν τροφὸς θάλπῃ τὰ ἑαυτῆς τέκνα

passages.text: We cared so deeply that we were delighted to share with you not only the gospel of God, but our own lives as well. That is how beloved you have become to us.
passages.sermon:
We are apostles of Christ.
We cared deeply for you.
We were happy to share the gospel of God with you.
We also shared our own lives with you.
You became very dear to us.
passages.original: οὕτως ὁμειρόμενοι ὑμῶν εὐδοκοῦμεν μεταδοῦναι ὑμῖν οὐ μόνον τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τοῦ Θεοῦ ἀλλὰ καὶ τὰς ἑαυτῶν ψυχάς διότι ἀγαπητοὶ ἡμῖν ἐγενήθητε

passages.text: Surely you recall, brothers, our labor and toil. We worked night and day so that we would not be a burden to anyone while we proclaimed to you the gospel of God.
passages.sermon:
Brothers, you remember our hard work and effort.
We worked during the night.
We worked during the day.
We did this so we would not be a burden to any of you.
While we worked, we preached the gospel of God to you.
passages.original: Μνημονεύετε γάρ ἀδελφοί τὸν κόπον ἡμῶν καὶ τὸν μόχθον νυκτὸς καὶ ἡμέρας ἐργαζόμενοι πρὸς τὸ μὴ ἐπιβαρῆσαί τινα ὑμῶν ἐκηρύξαμεν εἰς ὑμᾶς τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: You are witnesses, and so is God, of how holy, righteous, and blameless our conduct was among you who believed.
passages.sermon:
We lived among you who believe in Jesus Christ.
You saw how we acted.
God also saw how we acted.
We acted in a holy way.
We acted in a righteous way.
We acted in a blameless way.
You are witnesses to this.
God is also a witness to this.
passages.original: ὑμεῖς μάρτυρες καὶ ὁ Θεός ὡς ὁσίως καὶ δικαίως καὶ ἀμέμπτως ὑμῖν τοῖς πιστεύουσιν ἐγενήθημεν

passages.text: For you know that we treated each of you as a father treats his own children— encouraging you, comforting you, and urging you to walk in a manner worthy of God, who calls you into His own kingdom and glory.
passages.sermon:
We treated each of you as a father treats his own children.
We encouraged you.
We comforted you.
We urged you to live in a way that is worthy of God.
God calls you into His own kingdom and glory.
passages.original: καθάπερ οἴδατε ὡς ἕνα ἕκαστον ὑμῶν ὡς πατὴρ τέκνα ἑαυτοῦ παρακαλοῦντες ὑμᾶς καὶ παραμυθούμενοι καὶ μαρτυρόμενοι εἰς τὸ περιπατεῖν ὑμᾶς ἀξίως τοῦ Θεοῦ τοῦ καλοῦντος ὑμᾶς εἰς τὴν ἑαυτοῦ βασιλείαν καὶ δόξαν

passages.text: And we continually thank God because, when you received the word of God that you heard from us, you accepted it not as the word of men, but as the true word of God—the word which is now at work in you who believe.
passages.sermon:
We continually thank God.
You received the word of God from us.
You heard this word from us.
You did not accept it as the word of men.
You accepted it as the true word of God.
This word is now at work in you who believe.
passages.original: Καὶ διὰ τοῦτο καὶ ἡμεῖς εὐχαριστοῦμεν τῷ Θεῷ ἀδιαλείπτως ὅτι παραλαβόντες λόγον ἀκοῆς παρ’ ἡμῶν τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐδέξασθε οὐ λόγον ἀνθρώπων ἀλλὰ καθὼς ἀληθῶς ἐστὶν λόγον Θεοῦ ὃς καὶ ἐνεργεῖται ἐν ὑμῖν τοῖς πιστεύουσιν

passages.text: For you, brothers, became imitators of the churches of God in Judea that are in Christ Jesus. You suffered from your own countrymen the very things they suffered from the Jews, who killed both the Lord Jesus and their own prophets, and drove us out as well. They are displeasing to God and hostile to all men, hindering us from telling the Gentiles how they may be saved. As a result, they continue to heap up their sins to full capacity; the utmost wrath has come upon them.
passages.sermon:
You are brothers in Christ Jesus.
You became imitators of the churches of God in Judea.
Those churches are in Christ Jesus.
You suffered from your own countrymen.
Your suffering was the same as the suffering of those churches.
The Jews caused those churches to suffer.
The Jews killed the Lord Jesus.
The Jews killed their own prophets.
The Jews drove us out also.
They do not please God.
They are hostile to all people.
They stop us from speaking to the Gentiles.
They do not want the Gentiles to be saved.
They keep adding to their sins.
God’s wrath has come upon them fully.
passages.original: Ὑμεῖς γὰρ μιμηταὶ ἐγενήθητε ἀδελφοί τῶν ἐκκλησιῶν τοῦ Θεοῦ τῶν οὐσῶν ἐν τῇ Ἰουδαίᾳ ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ ὅτι τὰ αὐτὰ ἐπάθετε καὶ ὑμεῖς ὑπὸ τῶν ἰδίων συμφυλετῶν καθὼς καὶ αὐτοὶ ὑπὸ τῶν Ἰουδαίων τῶν καὶ τὸν Κύριον ἀποκτεινάντων Ἰησοῦν καὶ τοὺς προφήτας καὶ ἡμᾶς ἐκδιωξάντων καὶ Θεῷ μὴ ἀρεσκόντων καὶ πᾶσιν ἀνθρώποις ἐναντίων κωλυόντων ἡμᾶς τοῖς ἔθνεσιν λαλῆσαι ἵνα σωθῶσιν εἰς τὸ ἀναπληρῶσαι αὐτῶν τὰς ἁμαρτίας πάντοτε ἔφθασεν δὲ ἐπ’ αὐτοὺς ἡ ὀργὴ εἰς τέλος

passages.text: Brothers, although we were torn away from you for a short time (in person, not in heart), our desire to see you face to face was even more intense.
passages.sermon:
Brothers, we were separated from you for a short time.
We were apart from you in person.
We were not apart from you in heart.
We longed to see you very much.
We tried even harder to see you face to face.
passages.original: Ἡμεῖς δέ ἀδελφοί ἀπορφανισθέντες ἀφ’ ὑμῶν πρὸς καιρὸν ὥρας προσώπῳ οὐ καρδίᾳ περισσοτέρως ἐσπουδάσαμεν τὸ πρόσωπον ὑμῶν ἰδεῖν ἐν πολλῇ ἐπιθυμίᾳ

passages.text: For we wanted to come to you—indeed I, Paul, tried again and again—but Satan obstructed us.
passages.sermon:
Paul is writing to the brothers in Thessalonica.
Paul and his companions wanted to visit the Thessalonian believers.
Paul himself tried to come to them more than once.
Satan stopped them from coming.
passages.original: διότι ἠθελήσαμεν ἐλθεῖν πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἐγὼ μὲν Παῦλος καὶ ἅπαξ καὶ δίς καὶ ἐνέκοψεν ἡμᾶς ὁ Σατανᾶς

passages.text: After all, who is our hope, our joy, our crown of boasting, if it is not you yourselves in the presence of our Lord Jesus at His coming?
passages.sermon:
Paul wrote this letter to the Thessalonian believers.
Paul cared deeply for these believers.
Paul asked a question about hope, joy, and pride.
Paul said, "Who is our hope?"
Paul said, "Who is our joy?"
Paul said, "Who is our crown of boasting?"
Paul answered, "You are our hope, our joy, and our crown."
Paul said, "You will stand before our Lord Jesus when He comes."
Paul said, "You are our reason for hope, joy, and pride in Jesus' presence."
passages.original: τίς γὰρ ἡμῶν ἐλπὶς ἢ χαρὰ ἢ στέφανος καυχήσεως ἢ οὐχὶ καὶ ὑμεῖς ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ ἐν τῇ αὐτοῦ παρουσίᾳ

passages.text: You are indeed our glory and our joy.
passages.sermon:
Paul wrote this letter to the Thessalonian believers.
Paul cared deeply for these believers.
Paul said, “You are our glory.”
Paul also said, “You are our joy.”
passages.original: ὑμεῖς γάρ ἐστε ἡ δόξα ἡμῶν καὶ ἡ χαρά
